remaining_differences.what: Editor canvas: the reference has a photographic mountain and lake scene; the render uses a CSS landscape illustration.
Application chrome: the reference has window controls, a menu row, and a tab toolbar; these are missing from the render.
Slider area: the render retains the template’s bordered control panel and tick marks, unlike the reference’s simpler slider layout.

deviations: Slider labels, values, and instructions vary by seed, as required by the task.
report.notes: Small viewport and instruction-mode renders stayed on-screen. The oracle check passed.

differences: Application frame: the desktop title bar, window controls, menu row and large icon tabs are replaced by a compact web header and an unrelated left navigation sidebar.
Photo area: the detailed mountain and lake photograph is replaced by an abstract gradient with broad diagonal bands.

Task control: the large slider beneath the photo becomes a small bordered floating card, with a thin track, tiny handle, small inline label and extra tick labels. At the comparison size it crosses into the help panel instead of occupying the left column.
Page layout: the photo is much shallower, leaving a large empty central area; the task control is detached from the photo.
Help panel: headings, body text and icons are substantially smaller, with weak heading hierarchy and tiny bullet markers compared with the design.
Surface styling: the design's subtly shaded backgrounds and prominent blue and white slider handle are replaced by flatter dark surfaces and faint control borders.
frame_issues: The header, side-panel and notification instruction settings all display the same full-width instruction header and circular completion button; the panel and notification presentations are absent.
